I will keep my land in the usual winter wheat and summer maize rotation. In Quzhou County, that is the safest way for me to keep grain coming from the same field in one year, and I know this system well. I am 62, so I do not want to chase crops that need more hand labor or more market risk. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because I want stable yield, better stand, and less worry. For wheat, I will prepare the land with rotary tillage, put on enough nitrogen with phosphorus and potassium, water about three times if the season is normal, and spray about twice for weeds and disease. After wheat harvest, I will go straight into summer maize with no-tillage seeding to save time and moisture, then give fertilizer mainly to support ear growth, irrigate about twice if rain is not enough, and spray about twice for weeds and insects. I am choosing a steady grain plan, lower labor pressure, and methods I already trust.
